content.introduction: Asian stock markets experienced a second consecutive day of declines as tensions surrounding the Iran crisis heightened investor fears, pushing oil prices higher. Major regional indexes slipped due to concerns over potential supply disruptions, rising inflation, and the broader economic impact of prolonged geopolitical instability. Investors moved towards safe-haven assets, while shares in travel, energy-sensitive, and technology sectors faced renewed selling pressure. The BBC reported that South Korea and Thailand stock markets temporarily halted trading after plunging by more than 8%, triggering circuit breakers to avoid panic-selling. Meanwhile, CNBC noted mixed market performances with Japan's Nikkei 225 rising slightly, while South Korea's Kospi dropped.
body:
Asian stock markets declined for a second consecutive session as escalating tensions surrounding the Iran crisis rattled investor confidence and pushed oil prices higher. Major regional indexes slipped amid concerns over potential supply disruptions, rising inflation, and the broader economic impact of prolonged geopolitical instability. Investors shifted toward safe-haven assets while travel, energy-sensitive, and technology shares faced renewed selling pressure across key markets. Stock markets have fallen sharply since the US and Israel attacked Iran over the weekend, and many Asian stock markets have been hit particularly hard as the region imports large amounts of energy from the Middle East.

South Korea and Thailand stock markets were forced to temporarily halt trading after plunging by more than 8% and triggering so-called circuit breakers, which aim to avoid panic-selling. [...] # Stock markets and oil prices still volatile over fears Iran war may drag on

Getty Images Oil tanker 

UK and US stock markets rose but Asian indexes tumbled on Wednesday as oil and gas prices remained volatile over fears the US-Israel war with Iran may drag on.

The FTSE 100 index of the largest firms listed in London as well the big US and European indexes all rose on Wednesday following two days of sliding share prices, while several Asian indexes plummeted for a third day.

Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 0.28% to close at 71,250.06 after hitting a record high on Thursday, while the Topix lost 0.57% to end the trading day at 4,044.96.

South Korea's Kospi dropped 0.13% to close at 9,052.42, pulling back after crossing the 9,000 mark for the first time Thursday, while the small-cap Kosdaq declined 3.43%.

Shares of Samsung Electronics reversed earlier gains and fell 2.34%, while SK Hynix rose 2.94%. [...] Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.92%, ending the trading day at 8,828.7.

U.S., China, Hong Kong and Taiwan markets are closed for a holiday.

— Lee Ying Shan

Stocks of major Indian information technology companies fell as much as 7% on Friday after global professional service giant Accenture lowered its revenue guidance, souring sentiment toward the sector. [...] — Lim Hui Jie

Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 opened higher, advancing 0.6% after hitting a record high on Thursday, while the Topix opened flat.

South Korea's Kospi jumped 2.8% after crossing the 9,000 mark for the first time yesterday, while the small-cap Kosdaq slid 0.39%.

Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.74%.

China, Hong Kong and Taiwan markets are closed for a holiday.

— Lee Ying Shan
